title: tBTC is now exit-only on BOB, Optimism, and Polygon
summary: tBTC is now exit-only on BOB, Optimism, and Polygon, three chains with minimal tBTC activity.
body_markdown:
### What changed


As of November 19, 2026, tBTC is in exit-only mode on **BOB, Optimism and Polygon** , three chains with minimal tBTC activity. Bridging tBTC into these chains is disabled. Withdrawals are not affected: tBTC on these chains remains fully backed. If you hold tBTC on these chains, we recommend bridging back to Ethereum or another supported chain.


#### The cost of each network


Most of the work a network demands doesn’t depend on how much tBTC it holds. These costs grow with every network added, so a network holding a small share of supply needs the same baseline as one with heavy adoption:


- **Contract maintenance.** Gateways and tokens have to keep up with changes to the destination chain, its tooling and the messaging layer. Network upgrades, deprecated features and fee market changes all need review.
- **Messaging dependencies.** Each network takes on the configuration and operational risk of its messaging layer. Verifier sets, rate limits and pause controls have to be reviewed and kept correct over time.
- **Key and governance management.** Every deployment has admin roles and upgrade keys that must be held, rotated and audited.
- **Monitoring and alerting.** Supply invariants, relayer health, message latency and unusual mint or burn activity have to be watched on every network, around the clock.
- **Incident response.** Each network needs a tested pause procedure, a communications path, and people who know its specifics well enough to act quickly.
- **Reviews and audits.** Every change to shared code has to be checked against every deployment that uses it.


#### What exit-only mode means


- Bridging tBTC into these networks is disabled.
- **BOB:** exit via Chainlink CCIP. New transfers from Ethereum to BOB will revert.
- **Optimism and Polygon:** exit via Wormhole. Transfers into these chains now arrive as Wormhole-wrapped tBTC, not canonical tBTC. Please don’t bridge in.
- Redemption to BTC happens on Ethereum: bridge your tBTC out first, then redeem.
- tBTC already on each network stays fully backed. As holders exit, the bridged supply on that network shrinks to match.
- There is no exit deadline at this time, but we recommend bridging back to Ethereum or another supported network.


### Contract references


Contract addresses are listed in the[Threshold documentation](https://docs.threshold.network/contract-addresses/tbtc#l2-other-tbtc-application-contracts) . Always check addresses against the official documentation before interacting with them.
